 Montgomery County District Court
 Cause No. 2024-CV-0050
 Brandon Allen, Plaintiff, v. Harbor Point Mutual Auto Insurance, Defendant
 Defendant's Original Answer
Date:
5-21-24
Counsel for defendant:
Stephanie Williams, Ashford & Lyle LLP
Defendant generally denies each and every allegation contained in Plaintiff's Original Petition and demands strict
proof thereof as required by the Texas Rules of Civil Procedure. Pursuant to Rule 92, Defendant also asserts the
following affirmative defenses.
First, Plaintiff's alleged injuries were not proximately caused by the incident in question. The impact between the
vehicles was of low speed and minor force, and any condition Plaintiff now claims was pre-existing, degenerative, or
unrelated to the collision.
Second, Plaintiff failed to exercise ordinary care to mitiagte damages, including by failing to follow reasonable
medical advice and by incurring treatment that was unnecessary or unreasonable in cost. Any recovery must be
reduced accordingly.
Third, to the extent Plaintiff's own negligence contributed to the occurrence, Defendant invokes the proportionate
responsibility provisions of Chapter 33 of the Texas Civil Practice and Remedies Code. Any recovery must be
reduced by Plaintiff's percentage of responsibility, and bars recovery if that percentage exceeds fifty percent.
</page>

Person "role" must be one of: claimant, attorney, defense_attorney, expert, doctor, officer, adjuster, witness, other.
  claimant = the person who made the claim (also called patient, plaintiff, client, customer,
  or the driver who reported it). attorney = a lawyer for the claimant or plaintiff.
  defense_attorney = a lawyer for the insurance company or defendant.
Organization "type" must be one of: repair_shop, clinic, law_firm, court, insurer, police, other.
"policy_numbers" = only values labeled as a policy number. A claim number is not a policy number.
"street" and "city" = the person's own home address, only if the page gives it. Never use the
address of a clinic, shop, firm or court for a person.
"loss_dates" = only a date that the page clearly gives as the date of the accident, crash, loss or
injury. Do not list the date of a note, letter, report, visit, statement, filing or signature.
"words_before" = the words written on the page directly before that date, copied exactly, that say
it is the loss date. Examples: "Date of loss:", "Crash date:", "Date of injury:", "the collision on".
